findings.title: Network egress and the contract crate are guarded by prose, not tooling
findings.claim: The only crate with a tool-enforced dependency allow-list is the kernel. `store` and `extract` have a three-entry forbid-list (`reqwest`, `hyper`, `tokio`). `contract` and `planroom` have no external rule at all, and nothing lints `std::net` or `std::process` outside the kernel. So two rules that repo-layout.md presents as enforced are only conventions: "only `models` may use a network client" and the kernel's no-I/O rule, which can be bypassed through `contract`, the kernel's one workspace dependency.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, Boundaries: `store = { may_depend = ["contract"], external_forbid = ["reqwest", "hyper", "tokio"] }` (extract has the same line); `contract = { may_depend = [] }` and `planroom = {...}` carry no external rule. The boundary table claims "only `models` may use a network client | the same check". The "May depend on" lists for `contract`, `store`, `extract` and `planroom` exist only in the area table. They have already drifted: DR-72 adds `p256` to `planroom`, and the `planroom` row still lists only axum, tower-http, tokio, tokio-stream, tracing, anyhow and libc. The clippy no-I/O list is generated only for `crates/kernel/clippy.toml`. The check code (crates/xtask/src/boundaries.rs, check_crate_graph) applies `external_allow` only where one is set. KICKOFF R16: "Boundaries are enforced by tooling, not convention"; constraints: live calls gated behind an env flag, spend under $3. architecture.md "What leaves the machine" depends on every model or network call going through `models`' live gate and host allow-list.
findings.failure_scenario: An extract track adds `ureq` (a common synchronous HTTP client) to resolve a remote OpenAPI `$ref`, or calls `std::net::TcpStream` or `std::process::Command::new("curl")`. Every check passes. Scanned-repo content now leaves the machine with no `PLANROOM_LIVE_*` gate, no consent and no host allow-list. Separately, a helper `pub fn read(p) -> String { std::fs::read_to_string(p) }` added to `planroom-contract` and called from the kernel passes clippy, because the kernel's call site names `planroom_contract::read`, not `std::fs`. The kernel then does I/O with CI green.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `contract`, `store`, `extract` and `planroom` an `external_allow` in boundaries.toml covering normal and build dependencies. Generate the area table's "May depend on" cell from it, so the prose can't drift. Generate a clippy.toml with `disallowed-types`/`disallowed-methods` for `std::net::*` (and for `std::fs::*`/`std::process::*` in `contract`) for every crate except `models` and `planroom`. Allow `std::process::Command` only in the extract git-adapter module, through one checked `#[allow]` location. Add self-test plants: `ureq` in extract, `std::net::TcpStream::connect` in store, a `std::fs` wrapper in contract, `extract -> models` (a sideways crossing) and `testkit` as a normal dependency. Each must fail.

findings.title: A `skipped` check passes CI, so S15's gates can go silently unrun
findings.claim: Every xtask check can report `skipped (why)`. The design says only for `check audit` that a skip is a failure in CI. Nothing else defines whether a skip in CI fails the job, and the skeleton already exits 0 on skipped boundary plants and skipped test runners. Because `ci_runs_only_xtask` forbids any other CI step, nothing in CI can notice that the self-test, a plant, clippy on the copy, `claude plugin validate`, `cargo deny` or the installer's BusyBox step was skipped.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, The one task entry point: "prints one `ok`, `FAILED` or `skipped (why)` line per check". Only the `check audit` row says "locally `skipped (offline)` when it's down, in CI a failure". Skeleton: crates/xtask/src/boundaries.rs:481 `lines.push("skipped  a pack requires observability ...")` and then returns Ok; crates/xtask/src/main.rs:237 `skipped("cargo nextest run", "cargo-nextest is not installed; ran cargo test instead")`; main.rs:216 skips plugin validation. Toolchain pins: "ShellCheck and BusyBox ... sha256-pinned downloads in `xtask`" and the installer job runs on macos-15, where BusyBox ships no official binary (Iris runs BusyBox on Linux only, iris-release-bar.md line 87). KICKOFF R16: "A check in CI fails on any crossing". S15: "The boundary checks fail on a planted bad import". S14: "CI is green".
findings.failure_scenario: On a fresh runner, the self-test's offline pnpm install or the copy's clippy build can't run, or a pinned tool download is blocked. The step prints `skipped`, `cargo xtask check` exits 0, and the `check` job is green. S15 is then marked `passing` although no planted crossing was ever shown to fail. Likewise, `test --installer` on macos-15 skips BusyBox and S14's installer path is reported green without having run.
findings.proposed_fix: Make it a rule of the entry point that under `CI=true` every `skipped` is FAILED, unless the check name appears in a small committed allow-list (for example `ci_skips` in feature_list.json or xtask) that names the reason and the record that approved it. `feature_list_is_complete` should reject `passing` for any entry whose listed test or step was skipped on its CI path. Remove the nextest fallback in CI and say BusyBox is Linux-only (macOS runs `sh` and dash) instead of skipping it.

findings.title: "Plain `gen` writes every committed output" and the merge-conflict rule are wrong for golden files, eval results and `layout.lock`
findings.claim: Several committed generated outputs are not written by plain `cargo xtask gen`: `tests/golden/` (`--golden`, which runs the Rust tests), `packs/*/evals/*.result.json` (`cargo xtask eval`), `layout.lock` (`--layout-lock DR-n`, which refuses unless the record is newer) and `schema/baseline/`. Still, AGENTS.md and DR-70 tell agents to "take either side and run `cargo xtask gen`" on any generated-file conflict. No design text says the Rust tests compare against the committed golden files instead of writing them, so DR-6's "a contract drift fails both sides" has no defined drift check.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, gen row: "plain `gen` writes every committed output above". The Generated directories table lists `tests/golden/` under `gen --golden`, eval results under `cargo xtask eval` and `layout.lock` under `gen --layout-lock DR-n`. AGENTS.md, Working in this repository: "On a merge conflict in a generated file, take either side and run `cargo xtask gen`; never merge one by hand." contracts.md, Drift tests: only `golden_outputs_type_check` (types, not values). The Generated directories intro: "Each has ... a drift check". DR-6: "a contract drift fails both sides".
findings.failure_scenario: Two tracks change the same CLI output. On merge, the main agent takes one side of `tests/golden/cli/focus.json` and runs plain `gen`, which doesn't touch golden files. The mod tests in `target/mod-test` then pass against a stale envelope that no longer matches the engine. The mismatch first shows in S14 step 3, when an agent drives S1 and S2 through the plugin's tools. With a conflict in `layout.lock`, the same rule leaves `check layout` red, with no instruction that applies.
findings.proposed_fix: State that the golden-writing Rust tests compare by default and write only under `gen --golden`, and add `golden_outputs_equal_engine_output` to `cargo xtask test`. Rewrite the conflict rule per file: golden files use `gen --golden`, eval results use `cargo xtask eval`, `layout.lock` goes to the main agent with a new record, and everything else uses plain `gen`. Or make plain `gen` dispatch to each file's own generator.

findings.title: The decision-record gate gives tracks a red check whose fix command they're forbidden to run
findings.claim: A track that changes a gated surface can't make `cargo xtask check` pass. The state check fails and names `cargo xtask gen --layout-lock DR-n` as the fix, but AGENTS.md forbids tracks to run that command or write records, and nothing says how a workflow agent "asks" the main agent for a number mid-run. Numbers assigned up front also break when tracks merge out of order, because `gen --layout-lock` refuses a record that isn't newer than every record the lock already names.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, Decision-record gate: "fails on any difference, naming the fix: `cargo xtask gen --layout-lock DR-n`" and "`gen --layout-lock DR-n` refuses unless `## DR-n` ... is newer than every record the lock already names". AGENTS.md: "Only the main agent writes a record or runs `cargo xtask gen --layout-lock`; a track asks it for a record number" and "Run `cargo xtask check` ... before claiming success". KICKOFF process step 5: tracks verify each feature and commit; R16: the main agent records layout changes.
findings.failure_scenario: A track gets DR-81 and its sibling DR-80. The DR-81 track merges first. When the DR-80 track merges, `gen --layout-lock DR-80` is refused. Meanwhile, a track agent that sees `FAILED layout: run cargo xtask gen --layout-lock DR-n` either runs it with an invented number (the duplicate-heading check catches only exact duplicates) or reports its feature as failing and stalls.
findings.proposed_fix: In a linked worktree (`git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`), have `check layout` print "pending ratification: gated surfaces X, Y changed; the main agent records this at merge" as a distinct non-failing state, and have `gen --layout-lock` refuse there. Say that the main agent writes the record and the lock in the merge commit, so it doesn't pre-assign numbers, and drop the "a track asks for a number" step.

findings.title: Generated files aren't kept in marked directories, and several files are part generated, part hand-written
findings.claim: R16 asks for generated code in marked directories. The design puts generated outputs next to hand-written files: the mod bundle beside the hand-written `plugin/hooks/hooks.json`, `crates/kernel/clippy.toml`, `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` at the root, and table regions inside hand-written `docs/reference/errors.md` and `packs.md`, area `AGENTS.md` files and `plugin/scripts/engine.env`. `generated_read_only` and `.gitattributes` list only a few of these, so an agent can't tell from the path that a file is generated.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, Generated directories: `plugin/hooks/planroom-mod.js`, `plugin/scripts/engine.env` ("`gen` writes `PLANROOM_CATALOGUE_HASH`; `gen --version V` writes `PLANROOM_ENGINE_VERSION`", while `PLANROOM_REPO` has no generator), "`errors.md` tables", "each area's contract block". boundaries.toml `generated_read_only` lists three paths, and the current `.gitattributes` marks three. The drift test `generated_headers` covers only "every file in a generated directory". KICKOFF R16: "Generated code lives in marked directories and is never hand-edited."
findings.failure_scenario: An agent hand-edits a row in `docs/reference/errors.md` outside the generated tables, or changes `PLANROOM_REPO` in `engine.env`, which `gen` then rewrites or flags in a way the agent can't predict. Or an agent edits the mod bundle in `plugin/hooks/` because that directory also holds the hand-written `hooks.json`. Nothing at the directory level warned it.
findings.proposed_fix: Move whole generated files into marked directories: `plugin/hooks/generated/planroom-mod.js` (and point `hooks.json` at it), `plugin/types/` with a `GENERATED.md`, and the reference tables as `docs/reference/generated/*.md` included from the hand-written pages. Delimit the remaining mixed files (area `AGENTS.md`, `engine.env`) with BEGIN/END GENERATED markers. Generate `generated_read_only` and `.gitattributes` from the Generated directories table, and have `generated_headers` check every path in that table.

findings.title: The fixture's skill stays live agent context; `claudeMdExcludes` covers only CLAUDE.md files
findings.claim: DR-70 says the fixture's `CLAUDE.md` and its skill are live context for this repo's own sessions, but its only tooling fix is `claudeMdExcludes`, a setting for CLAUDE.md memory files. A-16 assumes the setting also hides `SKILL.md`, and the fallback is the prose rule in `examples/AGENTS.md`. Claude Code finds skills in nested `.claude/skills/` directories when an agent works on files beneath them, so `run-worker-tests` can show up as a project skill while an agent works on the extractors and the fixture.
findings.evidence: examples/fixture/repos/worker/07-run-tests-skill/tree/.claude/skills/run-worker-tests/SKILL.md exists. DR-70 Context: "The fixture's `CLAUDE.md` and skill are live agent context"; Decision: "`.claude/settings.json` lists the fixture's agent files in `claudeMdExcludes`". architecture.md A-16: if that doesn't hold, "the `examples/` area contract's rule ... is the only guard". The current `.claude/settings.json` has no exclusion of any kind. KICKOFF principle 2 ("context that is kept current") and R16 (tooling over convention).
findings.failure_scenario: An agent working on WS3 extractors reads the worker tree, gets `run-worker-tests` offered as a skill, and runs the fixture's test procedure, or follows its instructions, inside the Planroom repo instead of `cargo xtask test`.
findings.proposed_fix: Also add `permissions.deny: ["Skill(run-worker-tests)"]` to `.claude/settings.json`, or add a guardrails PreToolUse rule that denies a Skill call whose source path is under `examples/fixture/`, with a guardrails test. Have the WS8 check of A-16 test the skill path explicitly, not only the CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: Amended records keep superseded rules in their Decision bullets, and Read first points agents at them
findings.claim: Records are amended by appending "Amended in review round N" paragraphs that contradict the Decision bullets above them, and the Status still reads plain "accepted". The Read first lines send an agent resuming after a compaction straight to these records, so it can act on the superseded bullet.
findings.evidence: DR-59, Decision: "Dependabot waits 7 days" and "`cargo xtask gen --mod` also builds `target/mod-test/`"; its round 2 amendment: "Dependabot waits 14 days ... replacing `gen --mod`". DR-38, round 1: `.claude/settings.json` "sets the first two" variables; round 2: "sets only `PLANROOM_REPLAY=strict`". DR-60's last bullet ("or `PLANROOM_PACKS`") was voided by DR-62. repo-layout.md, Read first: `crates/xtask` → DR-38, DR-59, DR-70. KICKOFF release bar: "each fact in one place"; R16: conventions written down once.
findings.failure_scenario: After a compaction, a track that owns `crates/xtask` reads DR-59 as its Read first lines tell it to, implements `gen --mod` and a 7-day Dependabot cooldown, and the `release_pins` check (14 days) fails. Or the agent writes `PLANROOM_SPEND_LOG` into settings.json, which goes against DR-65.
findings.proposed_fix: Set an amended record's Status to "accepted, amended by DR-70 (round 2)". Rewrite its Decision bullets to the current rule and move the old text to a short History list. Or point the Read first table only at the current-state pages (repo-layout.md and architecture.md sections) and use records for rationale. Add a docs test that a record with an amendment paragraph has "amended" in its Status.

findings.title: Read first names two sections that don't exist, and neither Read first nor the directory map is checked or gated
findings.claim: Two Read first sections don't match any heading, and nothing checks that Read first names resolve. The directory map, the main navigation aid, isn't a gated surface, so it can drift from the area table and the tree with no record and no failing check.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, Read first: `crates/kernel` lists "The reconciler", but the heading is "### The reconciler (R7)" (anchor `#the-reconciler-r7`, which architecture.md:243 itself uses). `packages/canvas` lists "Remote mode through the Artifact", but the heading is "### Remote mode through the Artifact (S11)". The gated surfaces (Decision-record gate) include "the area contracts table on this page" but neither the Read first table nor the Directory map block. `area_contracts_match_repo_layout` checks only that the AGENTS.md blocks equal the table rows.
findings.failure_scenario: `cargo xtask gen` writes a broken link or an unfindable section name into `crates/kernel/AGENTS.md` and `packages/canvas/AGENTS.md`. An agent resuming after a compaction can't find the reconciler or remote-mode rules it is told to read first. Later, a heading rename or a moved directory leaves the map wrong while every check stays green.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate the Read first entries as links whose anchors `gen` resolves against the target page's headings, failing on a miss. Fix the two names. Add the Directory map's top two levels to the gated surfaces, or check them against `git ls-tree` the way the area table is checked.

findings.title: "Every directory has a stated purpose" is checked only at the top level and for `tests/*`, and the check's scope is unclear
findings.claim: R16's first bullet asks for a stated purpose for every directory. `area_contracts_match_repo_layout` covers only non-dot top-level directories and `tests/*`. It's also unclear whether `crates/`, `packages/` and `tests/` themselves need a row (only their children have rows), and whether untracked directories like `target/` and `node_modules/` count. New second-level directories, such as `crates/planroom/src/<new>/`, `packages/canvas/src/<new>/` or `tests/e2e/<new>/`, need neither a stated purpose nor a record.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, Area contracts: "Every non-dot top-level directory, and each `tests/*` directory, has a row, and `cargo xtask check` fails when one lacks a row or either file". The table has rows `crates/contract` ... but none for `crates`, `packages` or `tests`. `target/` and `node_modules/` are non-dot top-level directories in every working checkout. KICKOFF R16: "Every directory has a stated purpose."
findings.failure_scenario: Read literally against the filesystem, the check fails on every local run because `target/` has no row, so agents learn to ignore it. Read leniently, a track adds `crates/planroom/src/sync/` beside `server/` and `app/`. No document says what it owns, and the next agent puts Artifact sync code in a third place.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the check over `git ls-files` directories. State that `crates/`, `packages/` and `tests/` are containers whose children are the areas. Require every tracked directory down to depth 3 (excluding `examples/fixture/**` and generated directories) to appear in the Directory map or in a generated "Layout" block in its area's AGENTS.md, with a check that fails on a missing entry.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The only crate with an external allow-list is the kernel. `store` and `extract` forbid three named crates. `contract`, `models` and `planroom` have no external rule, and nothing lints `std::net` or `std::process` outside the kernel. So `ureq` in extract, or a `std::net` call in store or extract, passes every check the design lists. The table still claims "only `models` may use a network client" is enforced by "the same check". The no-I/O rule in the contract row ("Must not: ... I/O") has no tool behind it, which leaves a bypass of the kernel's lint through a contract helper. The `planroom` row has also drifted: DR-72 adds `p256`, which the row doesn't list. This goes against KICKOFF R16 ("Boundaries are enforced by tooling, not convention") and weakens the live-call gate, so it stays material.
verdicts.evidence: repo-layout.md:157-163: `contract = { may_depend = [] }`, `store = { may_depend = ["contract"], external_forbid = ["reqwest", "hyper", "tokio"] }` (extract has the same line), and `models` and `planroom` have no external rule. repo-layout.md:201: "only `models` may use a network client | the same check, with each crate's `external_forbid`". repo-layout.md:200: the clippy no-I/O list is only in `crates/kernel/clippy.toml`. repo-layout.md:99: the contract row's Must not includes "I/O" and names no enforcement. decisions.md:1570 (DR-72): "`planroom` gains the `p256` crate". repo-layout.md:104: the planroom row omits p256. decisions.md:1184 (DR-59): "`store` and `extract` may not depend on a network client". That is a forbid-list, not an allow-list. KICKOFF.md:117.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The design defines `skipped (why)` for every check, but only `check audit` says a skip fails in CI. No rule says what a skip means in CI for the self-test steps, the plugin validation, nextest or the BusyBox step. And `ci_runs_only_xtask` means no other CI step could catch one. The skeleton already returns Ok after a skipped plant, and the pack-plant step that S15 needs is printed as skipped. BusyBox has no official macOS binary, yet `test --installer` runs on macos-15 with BusyBox `sh`. A green CI could therefore hide a gate that never ran, including S15's planted crossings. That conflicts with R16 ("A check in CI fails on any crossing"). Some of this is a guess about future behaviour, but by the uphold-when-uncertain rule it stays material.
verdicts.evidence: repo-layout.md:258: "prints one `ok`, `FAILED` or `skipped (why)` line per check". repo-layout.md:265: only the audit row says "locally `skipped (offline)` when it's down, in CI a failure". repo-layout.md:229 and contracts.md:16 say "fails the check, never skips it" for those two checks only. crates/xtask/src/boundaries.rs:481 pushes "skipped  a pack requires observability ...", then returns `Ok(lines)` when `failures` is empty. crates/xtask/src/main.rs:237 skips nextest, and main.rs:216 skips plugin validate. repo-layout.md:267 (`--installer` runs ShellCheck, BusyBox `sh`) and :335 (`installer (os)` on ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15).
